schema.title: O*NET occupation title
schema.riasec: [R,I,A,S,E,C] numeric interest scores 1-7, or null if code-only
schema.high_point_code: verified 1-3 letter Holland high-point interest code (interest signal used by career_match.py when riasec is null)
schema.job_zone: O*NET Job Zone (int 3/4/5); '1-2' string for the grouped low-prep tier
schema.source_url: O*NET OnLine Browse-by-Interests page where the code was observed
schema.work_values: {value_name: rank 1-6} ipsative ranking (1=most important) over the six O*NET Work Values, or null
schema.work_values_extent_1_7: raw 1-7 Extent scores the ranking was derived from (audit)
schema.work_values_db: O*NET DB release Work Values came from

notes.riasec_null: Numeric 1-7 RIASEC scores are not exposed on O*NET OnLine's public occupation/browse pages (they live in the downloadable O*NET Interests DB). Every occupation therefore carries riasec:null and its VERIFIED high_point_code carries the interest signal. No score was invented.
notes.job_zone_mixed_type: job_zone is an integer for Zones 3/4/5; O*NET groups the lowest-prep tier as 'Job Zone 1-2', so those entries use the string '1-2' rather than a fabricated single number.
notes.mapped_terms: Terms with no dedicated O*NET-SOC code were mapped to the nearest real code and disclosed, not fabricated: 'medical physicist'/'MRI physicist' -> Physicists 19-2012.00; 'machine learning / AI engineer' -> Data Scientists 15-2051.00 and Computer and Information Research Scientists 15-1221.00.
notes.omitted: Generic trades (electricians, plumbers, carpenters, welders, machinists) whose codes were not returned in the fetched page listings were OMITTED rather than guessed.
notes.numeric_riasec_upgrade: 51 occupations now carry REAL numeric O*NET Occupational-Interest scores (1-7, element 1.B.1, DB 30.3 career_interest_types.csv, 02/2026); the remaining 137 stay high-point-code-only (riasec:null, scored via the disclosed 3-2-1 expansion, lower confidence). Nothing invented.
notes.work_values: 46 occupations carry Work Values as an ipsative rank (1=most important) derived from the six 1-7 Extent scores (element 1.B.2, DB 30.2 - last release to publish Work Values; discontinued in 30.3). work_values_extent_1_7 keeps the raw scores for audit. Occupations O*NET does not rate carry work_values:null, NOT estimated.

scale_note: riasec_scores are O*NET Occupational Interests (data element 1.B.1.a-f, scale OI) on a 1-7 scale (higher = stronger interest), from O*NET Database 30.3 (career_interest_types.csv, dated 02/2026, Domain Source Machine Learning/Expert). high_point_code is O*NET's own First/Second/Third Interest High-Point (elements 1.B.1.g/h/i, scale IH), mapped 1=R,2=I,3=A,4=S,5=E,6=C (0 = no further high-point); verified against argmax of the numeric scores for 922/923 occupations. work_values.extent_scale_1_7 are the six O*NET Work Values (element 1.B.2.a-f, scale EX Extent) on a 1-7 scale; work_values.high_point is the First/Second/Third Work Value High-Point (elements 1.B.2.g/h/i, scale VH). Work Values come from O*NET Database 30.2 - the LAST release to include Work Values (discontinued in 30.3) - so they are ~one release older than the interests data.
coverage_note: 68 occupations, all six RIASEC interest areas represented, densely weighted toward the user's data-science/ML/research/computing/medical-imaging field plus a broad spread across healthcare, skilled trades (Realistic), arts (Artistic), social services/education (Social), business/sales/law (Enterprising) and admin/finance (Conventional). Numeric RIASEC (1-7) and high-point codes were fetched for ALL 68. Work Values were fetched for 62; 6 newer/reorganized SOC codes are not rated for Work Values in O*NET 30.2 and have work_values = null (Data Scientists 15-2051.00, Software Developers 15-1252.00, Web & Digital Interface Designers 15-1255.00, Project Management Specialists 13-1082.00, Financial & Investment Analysts 13-2051.00, Sales Representatives of Services 41-3091.00).
work_values_discontinuation_note: O*NET Work Values were fully DISCONTINUED in the current O*NET Database 30.3 (no 1.B.2 elements in the 30.3 content model; work_values.csv returns HTTP 404 for 30.3 and all older CSV releases). The numeric Work Values here are therefore sourced from Database 30.2, the last release that published them (per the O*NET “What’s New” notice: Tools Used and Work Values are no longer updated; use the 30.2 files). No fabricated values are included: the 6 occupations without a 30.2 Work Values rating are returned as work_values = null rather than estimated.
